title:
From report chasing
to a clearer daily picture.
body: Teach a workflow once. Keep the proof. Put answers beside the dashboard.
notes: Introduce Aimsigh as our local prototype for Goodwill. All displayed records are synthetic. Labor and shipping inputs are invented demonstration assumptions. The live showcase has no external model or production Teams connection.

title:
The dashboard problem
starts before the dashboard.
body: Amanda needs reports to arrive. Debie needs dependable visibility. Manual retrieval and consolidation connect the two.

cards.title: Amanda
cards.text: Upright is the repeated, date-changing task. Her 30–45 minute estimate includes interruptions.

cards.title: The handoff
cards.text: Reports feed Excel, Sonia’s summary and existing Power BI. Compatible delivery matters.

cards.title: The commitment
cards.text: Amanda’s nonbinding LOI expresses interest. Access, a pilot and purchase are not approved.

notes: We spoke with operational stakeholders and technical mentors rather than starting with charts. Amanda now has an assistant; support cannot depend on the departed e-commerce manager. Cite the interview estimate, not measured savings. The founder deck describes nonbinding interest; do not imply that the scanned LOI establishes a purchased or authorized production pilot.

title:
Bring fragmented reports
into a controlled workflow.
body: Share acquisition mechanisms. Keep source meaning, parsing and overlap rules specific.
notes: Nine reports are not nine revenue feeds. Upright and Cash Monkey are connected local replicas. Jewelry, shipping expenses, marketplace reports and settlement summaries have different meanings. The other seven are fixture examples or await approved access. We do not sum their amounts into our showcase revenue.

title:
Teach the task once.
Change the dates next time.
body: Reports → Paid orders → Dates → Generate → Ready → Download.

cards.title: Record
cards.text: Actual local DOM actions and date parameters.

cards.title: Review
cards.text: A bounded recipe with an explicit operator approval.

cards.title: Replay
cards.text: Real browser execution and a verified CSV artifact.

notes: Open the live showcase Collect view. This is a screenshot-informed, functioning simulated portal. Restricted Upright API access is reported; the commercial reason is not confirmed. We are not bypassing a provider restriction. Model-free replay is distinct from optional probabilistic Jev decisions.

title:
Amanda shows
the workflow.
body: Record September 29. Review the captured actions. Approve the recipe before replay.
image_caption: Actual local recorder and simulated portal
notes: Perform the task in the embedded portal: navigate to the report, fill both dates, generate, wait for ready and download. Stop recording and review accessible control labels and parameter bindings. Approve the recipe. The recording is captured from user actions; it is not a video presented as a recorder. If the live state is unavailable, identify this screenshot as a previously verified capture.

title:
New dates.
The same reviewed task.
body: Replay September 30 for Upright, then Cash Monkey. Watch genuine browser frames and import evidence.
image_caption: Actual replay frames and verified collection result
notes: The rehearsal is already seeded through September 29. September 30 collection completes the month. Explain collection, verification, import and publication as separate states. Source records are explicitly disjoint in this fictional sample; this is not a claim that real marketplace reports never overlap. Cash Monkey unit rows and order counts retain their separate grains.

title:
A changed page
needs an explicit decision.
body: A mismatched control stops replay. The operator reviews and approves a new recipe. Last-good data stays available.

cards.title: Bounded execution
cards.text: Known local destinations and permitted operations.

cards.title: No bad publication
cards.text: Wrong dates, missing reports or failed checks cannot become new financial totals.

cards.title: Jev is conditional
cards.text: Probabilistic decision adapter is a future approved option. Main demo is model-free.

notes: Demonstrate changed-label mode if time permits, then show the reviewed repair path. Do not claim that automation works forever or that typed AI output is financially correct. A separate scripted Jev mockup is not a real model call. No credentials or provider approval have been assumed.

title:
One published snapshot.
Every result keeps its lineage.
body: Raw file → staging → versioned sales → published rows → snapshot → workbook, charts and answers.
notes: This diagram reflects the actual Python/SQLite implementation. source_files archive checksummed bytes; import_batches and staging_rows retain reconciliation; sale_versions and metric_run_rows pin published records. Showcase snapshots pin both source publications and versioned labor/shipping inputs. A hosted PostgreSQL system is a future deployment choice, not what is running here.

title:
Give Amanda
a usable workbook.
body: A monthly summary, 30 daily tabs, normalized records, modeled inputs and source evidence—all from the same snapshot.
image_caption: Preview rendered from the actual exported XLSX values
notes: Download the workbook from the application. Open it in Excel if available or use the supplied preview, which reads the real exported OOXML cells. Show the monthly summary, a daily tab and source evidence. Backend calculations and cached workbook values reconcile. This output is not the approved month-end allocation workbook or a Business Central posting file. CSV plus a dictionary offers a bridge to existing Power BI.

title:
Sales are measured.
The model is disclosed.
body: Demo net sales = item sales − refunds. Shipping collected, taxes and fees are excluded from that metric.

cards.title: Labor assumptions
cards.text: Upright: 2 h/store/day, then 3 h from Sept 24. Cash Monkey: 0.5 h/store/day.

cards.title: Cost assumptions
cards.text: Source fees; invented $3.50 shipping/record and $20/h labor.

cards.title: Contribution margin
cards.text: Net sales less fees, modeled shipping and labor. Excludes overhead and taxes.

notes: Missing inputs remain unavailable. Contribution margin is a demonstration measure, not approved production net margin. Labor is allocated by source/store/day, not platform; a platform filter therefore makes labor-dependent metrics unavailable. Distinct customers retain supported source/platform scopes. The August inventory example is separately dated and is never joined to these September sales.

title:
The charts follow
the verified data.
body: Daily trends, source and store breakdowns, productivity, coverage and freshness share the selected snapshot.
notes: Open Understand. Change a source or store filter and show the chart/cards/evidence updating together. Explain what the chart can and cannot establish. September sell-through, year-over-year growth and production net margin remain unavailable without their required inputs. Inventory examples use their own August view. This is our local dashboard, not a native Power BI or Superset deployment.

eyebrow: LIVE · A COMPARISON YOU CAN INSPECT
title:
Revenue rose.
Modeled hours rose faster.
body: The productivity comparison uses matched sales and invented labor inputs across two seven-day periods.
notes: The intended controls are net sales $60,727.56 / 420 hours = $144.59 per hour, versus $61,706.64 / 588 hours = $104.94 per hour. Show the values returned by the final tested application. This demonstrates an arithmetic driver in fictional data. It does not prove real staffing inefficiency or a causal business explanation. Source filters apply to both periods consistently.

eyebrow: LIVE · ANSWERS WHERE THE TEAM WORKS
title:
“Why is revenue
per labor hour down?”
body: A Teams-style local channel answers supported questions with deterministic tools, periods, definitions and evidence links.
image_caption: Actual model-free local conversation beside its dashboard
notes: Ask the productivity question, follow a source citation and open labor input evidence. Then show an unsupported question returning supported alternatives rather than inventing a number or cause. The channel is a local prototype, not a Teams tenant integration. Answers use tested metrics/comparison/evidence tools and templates, with no Copilot, LLM, RAG or external model call. A real Copilot/Teams adapter requires tenant and security approval.

title:
Fit the workflow
to Goodwill’s tools.
body: Validate one authorized source in parallel with current reporting. Reuse Excel and Power BI before choosing new infrastructure.

cards.title: Approve the inputs
cards.text: Report authority, overlap, real formats, definitions and access.

cards.title: Fit Microsoft
cards.text: Workbook consumption, Power BI, identity, tenant policy and optional Copilot/Teams.

cards.title: Own the operation
cards.text: Measure handling time and reliability. Name support, rollback and acceptance owners.

notes: Nonbinding LOI interest is the starting point, not approval to deploy. Managed databases and Superset are alternatives with hosting/maintenance requirements, not guaranteed faster or free operation. Accounting-close automation requires separate finance mappings, validation and approval. We have not measured ROI. Pilot success needs a baseline and named process/IT owners.

title:
Teach the task.
Keep the proof.
Understand the number.
body: Local synthetic showcase · verified sample inputs · downloadable workbook · evidence-backed supported answers.
notes: Close with what the working application showed. Offer the code, workbook, HTML/PDF/PowerPoint deck and narrated recorded walkthrough. The backup video is labelled as a recording. Final human acceptance and organizer submission are separate. Repository: github.com/joconne8/sprinthack-nd-2026.
